title: Onboarding Experiments and Fidelity-Cost Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
This playbook describes how we run experiments when onboarding new developer customers to Redwood Inference, with a clear mapping between fidelity profiles, cost signals, and SLA entitlements. The aim is to keep developer friction low while making unit economics predictable and measurable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Audience
- Product managers and go-to-market leads running onboarding pilots
- Solutions engineers and customer success teams handling migrations
- Platform engineers building fidelity policy controls and telemetry

Scope and intent
- Defines onboarding experiment cohorts (A/B/C) tied to fidelity presets and priced trial credits.
- Sets measurable criteria for moving customers between fidelity tiers.
- Covers rollout steps, required product hooks, billing implications, and rollback guidance.

Definitions
- Fidelity profile: a named bundle of runtime characteristics (model variant, quantization level, batching limits, streaming vs chunked responses).
- Onboarding credit: time-limited usage credit applied to a tenant to cover trial costs.
- Entitlement SLA: the latency and availability guarantees attached to a pricing tier.

High-level approach
1) Three onboarding cohorts:
   - Cohort A (Exploratory): high-fidelity default model, minimal batching, extended latency budget (200ms p50 target), 1,000 onboarding credits.
   - Cohort B (Balanced): mid-fidelity variant (int8 or mixed precision), moderate batching, standard latency budget (120ms p50), 2,000 onboarding credits.
   - Cohort C (Economy): quantized variant with aggressive batching and prefix-caching, tight cost limits, relaxed p50 latency (220ms), 5,000 onboarding credits to show the cost savings.

2) Instrument: telemetry for per-request fidelity tags, credit burn-rate, per-route latency distribution, and quality regressions measured against shadow-eval prompt sets.

3) Gate graduation: customers must hit usage and quality thresholds in their cohort for N days before they are promoted automatically, per the Fidelity Promotion Rule (FPR).

Fidelity Promotion Rule (FPR)
- Inputs (last 7 days): 1) Daily active tokens >= 10k, 2) Regression rate against shadow prompts <= 1.2x baseline, 3) Average credit burn per 1k tokens within the cohort budget.
- All inputs met for 7/7 days -> promote to the next fidelity tier.
- Regression above 2x baseline for 3 consecutive days -> roll back to the prior tier immediately and open a fidelity incident.

Required product hooks (implementation checklist)
- Tenant metadata: onboarding_cohort, onboarding_start, onboarding_credits_remaining (API + Console).
- Runtime: fidelity_tag header on inference requests, mapped to model variant and quantization profile.
- Billing: trial credit ledger entries and reporting APIs for credit burn by route/model.
- Observability: dashboard for cohort distribution, credit velocity, p50/p95 latency, and shadow-eval regression trend.
- Admin tooling: manual promotion/rollback override with an audit log (who/when/why).

Experiment matrix (example)
(Text table here; build as a dashboard table in Console)
| Cohort | Model Variant | Quant | Batch Size | p50 Target | Trial Credits | Expected unit cost delta vs baseline |
| Cohort A | redwood-xl-v2 | fp16 | 1-2 | 200ms | 1k | +45% |
| Cohort B | redwood-xl-v2-mix | int8-mix | 4-8 | 120ms | 2k | +5% |
| Cohort C | redwood-xl-quant | int8-q | 16-64 | 220ms | 5k | -60% |

Pricing and packaging implications
- Trial credits are non-billable ledger items that expire at onboarding_end + 30 days.
- Usage beyond the trial converts to regular billing at the tenant's chosen pricing tier.
- Cohort-specific uplift: customers who stay on Cohort A after the trial pay a 10% fidelity surcharge for the higher unit cost; Cohort C conversions receive a 5% low-fidelity discount.

Quick decision table
- Regulated private deployment (VPC / on-prem): default to Cohort B unless there is an explicit cost-savings mandate; run Cohort C only after security review.
- Quality complaints within the first 72 hours: escalate to the CSM; consider a one-time temporary credit and an immediate move to higher fidelity for diagnosis.

PRD requirements (minimal viable set for Q4 onboarding pilots)
- PRD-1: New tenant fields (onboarding_cohort, onboarding_expires_at, onboarding_credits) in the Accounts API and Console.
- PRD-2: Fidelity tags in the inference API, with the mapping stored in Variant Catalog.
- PRD-3: Credit burn reporting pipeline with hourly aggregation and tenant-level export.
- PRD-4: Shadow-eval integration that runs 2% of requests through shadow variants and surfaces regression alerts in the Console.
- PRD-5: Console cohort visualization plus manual override controls with audit trail.

Design constraints and non-goals
- No per-request model switching beyond fidelity_tag during onboarding; promotion is staged at tenant level only.
- No new pricing SKUs during the pilot; we rely on credit accounting plus simple surcharges/discounts.

Telemetry and SLOs
- Required telemetry spans: fidelity_tag, model_variant, quant_profile, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_latency_ms, shadow_eval_result (pass/fail), credit_delta.
- Pilot SLOs: 99.5% of cohort B requests meet p50 latency <= 120ms; 99% meet p95 <= 400ms.

Rollout plan and milestones
- Week 0 (prep): tenant metadata and variant mapping.
- Week 2 (alpha): Cohort C enabled for 5 internal customers with 72 hours of synthetic traffic.
- Week 4 (beta): 10 developer customers invited through the self-serve onboarding flow; monitor credit burn and quality regressions.
- Week 8 (pilot review): cohort-level economics analysis and a proposal for formal pricing adjustments.
- Week 12 (expand): automated graduation rules and cohort-aware defaults in Console templates.

KPIs and success criteria
- Onboarding-to-paid conversion rate >= 15% within 60 days for pilot customers.
- Average cost per 1k tokens for converted customers not > 25% of projections for the Cohort B baseline.
- Shadow-eval regression alert rate < 1% for promoted tenants.

Rollback and incident playbook
1) Detection: a regression alert pages on-call and informs the CSM.
2) Immediate action: switch the tenant back to the prior fidelity_tag, revoke the promotion, and issue one-time debugging credits.
3) Postmortem: attach shadow-eval logs, sample prompts, token-level traces, and latency and burn-rate time series.

Billing and finance checklist
- Finance approves the pilot's credit-expense budget and gets weekly burn rate updates.
- Use a dedicated accounting tag for onboarding credits so promotional cost is tracked separately.

Console UX notes (developer-facing)
- Onboarding banner in Console showing cohort, credits remaining, expected upgrade path, and an optional one-click request to talk to an SE.
- Timeline view counting down to automatic promotion or expiry.

Sample API mapping snippet (tenant metadata update)
{ "tenant_id": "acct_12345", "onboarding_cohort": "cohort_b", "onboarding_credits": 2000, "onboarding_expires_at": "2028-07-20T00:00:00Z" }

Open questions and recommended experiments
- Should promotions be rate-limited to avoid capacity spikes? Recommendation: stagger promotions in a rolling window (max 5% of tenants per hour).
- What trial credit size works best per industry? Recommendation: a 3-month A/B test with stratified sampling by ARR and expected daily tokens.
